title: Express.js Revision Notes: Setup, Routing, Middleware and Routers
summary: Quick revision of Express from app setup through routes, request and response objects, the middleware chain, built-in and third-party middleware, and routers. It ends with common mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Express Mental Model and App Setup
points: Definition: Express is a thin Node HTTP layer. An app is a function (req, res) that pushes each request through an ordered stack of middleware and route handlers
Mental model: request in, the first matching layer runs, and it either ends the response or calls next() to pass on; if nothing responds, Express returns a 404
Minimal app: const app = express(); app.get('/', (req, res) => res.send('hi')); app.listen(3000, () => console.log('up'))
Setup order matters: body parsers and global middleware first, then routes, then a 404 handler, then the error handler last
app.set('trust proxy', 1) when behind a proxy or load balancer so req.ip and req.protocol are correct; app.disable('x-powered-by') hides the header

chapters.title: Routes, Params and Query Strings
points: Route shape: app.METHOD(path, ...handlers). app.all() matches every method and app.use() matches by path prefix

Route params: '/users/:id' gives req.params.id, and it is always a string, so convert with Number(). Optional params are ':id?' in Express 4; Express 5 writes '/users{/:id}', and ':id?' throws at startup
Query string: '/search?q=js&page=2' gives req.query = { q: 'js', page: '2' }. Query values are strings too, and repeated keys become arrays
Routes match in registration order and the first match wins, so put specific routes like '/users/me' before '/users/:id'
app.route('/books').get(list).post(create) chains the methods for one path; router.param('id', fn) preloads a param for every route on that router that uses it (use app.param for routes on app)

chapters.title: Request and Response Objects
points: Request fields: req.params (path), req.query (URL), req.body (needs a parser), req.headers (lowercase keys), req.get('Header'), req.method, req.path, req.originalUrl, req.ip

res.send(x) sends a string, buffer or object. res.json(obj) sends JSON with Content-Type set. res.status(201).json(obj) chains. res.sendStatus(404) sends the status text ('Not Found') as the body; a 204 is sent with no body
res.redirect(302, '/login'), res.set('X-Id', '1'), res.cookie('sid', v, { httpOnly: true }) and res.sendFile(absPath) cover the other common responses
res.locals and req.<custom> carry per-request data between middleware, for example req.user set by an auth middleware

A response ends with send, json, end, redirect, sendFile or sendStatus (res.set, res.status and res.cookie do not end it). Sending a second time throws 'Cannot set headers after they are sent', so always return after responding early

chapters.title: Middleware Chain, next() and Error Handling
points: Middleware is a function (req, res, next). It can change req or res, end the response, or call next() to hand control to the next layer
Order is execution order. app.use(fn) runs for every request and app.use('/api', fn) only for that prefix; each layer must respond or call next(), or the request hangs
next(err) skips ahead to error middleware. Error handlers take four arguments (err, req, res, next) and are registered after all routes
Async handlers: Express 5 forwards rejected promises to the error handler. Express 4 needs try/catch with next(err) or a wrapper, because a throw inside an async function is not caught
Mistakes: forgetting next() so the request hangs, calling next() after responding, putting express.json() after the routes so req.body is undefined, and an error handler that is not the last layer

chapters.title: Built-in, Third-Party Middleware and Routers
points: Built-in: express.json() and express.urlencoded({ extended: true }) populate req.body; express.static('public') serves files; the body size limit defaults to 100kb and is set with { limit }
Common third-party: cors() for cross-origin access, helmet() for security headers, morgan('dev') for request logs, cookie-parser for req.cookies; install with npm i and add with app.use()
Router: const router = express.Router(); router.get('/:id', handler); export it and mount with app.use('/users', router). Paths inside the router are relative to the mount point
Router-level middleware: router.use(auth) protects only that router, and a handler can take middleware inline: app.get('/admin', auth, handler)
Mistakes: no body parser so req.body is undefined, wide-open cors() in production, route order that shadows a router, and secrets or stack traces leaking through the error handler

chapters.title: Express Cheat Sheet
points: Setup order: express() then middleware (json, cors, helmet) then routers then 404 handler then error handler then listen
Handlers: req.params.id, req.query.q, req.body.x; reply with res.status(n).json(obj); every middleware calls next() or responds
Status codes: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 bad input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 500 server error
Router mount: app.use('/api/users', usersRouter); error handler signature: (err, req, res, next); param values are always strings
Final checklist: parser before routes, specific routes before dynamic ones, return after responding, error handler last, async errors forwarded to next(err)
